goal: Record the rejection of job_outbox-boundary enforcement for Import consent as ADR 0016, and make guardImportConsent's refusals separable by SQL — for the 7-day job_outbox archival window — by completing the refused outbox row with completion_reason = 'import_consent_blocked'.
non_goals: No job_outbox trigger, CHECK constraint, or migration — the Import consent enforcement locus stays ZernioBackfillWorker per spec §5.3, re-affirmed by ADR 0016.
No change to guardImportConsent's proceed/skip decision, its sql.begin serialization, its businesses FOR UPDATE lock, or the importConsentStateSql derived-expiry predicate.
No per-state reason values — one 'import_consent_blocked' member; the specific refusal state (pending | declined | expired | missing) stays in the existing structured log line.
No HealthAlertPoller check, no Sentry capture, no PostHog event — a refusal is the guard working, not an incident.
No /admin/jobs rendering of completion_reason; SURFACE stays backend.
No completion_reason on guardZernioJobEligibility's three skips (missing row, archived location, subscription guard) — they stay generic completions.
No change to owner_unreachable's PERSISTED VALUE, its two poller readers, or the tenant-scope allowlist entries that spell its SQL. Only the writing helper's name and signature change.
No backfill of historical rows; legacy and other-topic rows keep completion_reason NULL.

No modification of worker/__tests__/helpers/mock-sql.ts — distinguishing the tx handle from the outer sql client in a unit test would require changing a helper shared by many suites, for a property already proven against real Postgres by the integration suite's forced-race test.
user_visible_behavior: None for owners — no UI, no notification, no API shape change.

Operator-visible only: a zernio_initial_backfill outbox row refused by guardImportConsent now carries job_outbox.completion_reason = 'import_consent_blocked' instead of NULL, so a policy refusal is separable by SQL from a genuine completed import.
invariants: Invariant #2 (transactional outbox): the reason write happens inside guardImportConsent's existing sql.begin on the same tx handle as the businesses FOR UPDATE — never a second statement outside that transaction.
Spec §5.3 single-owner: importConsentStateSql stays the ONE spelling of the derived-expiry predicate — nothing re-spells it in SQL, PL/pgSQL, or a migration.
Import consent stays fail-closed: only 'accepted' proceeds; every other state and a missing businesses row are skip-as-success (outbox row completed, never failed, thrown, or retried).
#679's data-loss window stays closed: the businesses row lock and the in-transaction outbox completion remain both load-bearing.
owner_unreachable's PERSISTED VALUE is unchanged and pinned against live Postgres — same emitted UPDATE, same attempt-guarded CAS, same 0-row warn, same two poller readers.

completion_reason values are written and read only via OUTBOX_COMPLETION_REASON — no bare string literal at any site, tests included (CLAUDE.md working rules). EXACTLY ONE exception, recorded here so it is not read as a violation: the wire-value contract test ('OUTBOX_COMPLETION_REASON preserves the persisted owner_unreachable wire value') compares the constant TO a literal, which is its entire purpose — a vocabulary whose every reader resolves the same constant cannot otherwise detect a renamed value stranding historical rows.
edge_cases: Superseded dispatch attempt: the reason write uses the same attempt-guarded dispatchedRow CAS, so a stale attempt updates 0 rows and warns rather than stamping a reason onto a newer attempt's row.

Missing businesses row (reason 'missing'): still marked import_consent_blocked — a hand-inserted row for a deleted location is a refusal, not a separate class. Note this is also the case where the refusal state is NOT recoverable from the businesses row, so the log line is the only per-state record.

Guard-first-then-owner-accepts interleaving (#679): the refused row completes WITH the marker and recordImportDecisionAndEnqueue inserts a fresh runnable row; the marker sits on the old row id and must not make the fresh row look pre-refused.

A row refused as 'pending' whose business later becomes 'accepted': completion_reason stays 'import_consent_blocked' on the historical row — it records that a refusal happened, not current state, and the state at refusal time is NOT re-derivable from the business row afterwards.
checkOwnerUnreachable's `completion_reason IS DISTINCT FROM 'owner_unreachable'` predicate must not be perturbed by a new non-NULL value appearing on a different topic.

Legacy rows refused BEFORE this change keep completion_reason NULL, so NULL does not universally mean 'genuine import' — the operator query is reliable only for post-deployment refusals, and ADR 0016 must say so.
Every other one of the 32 topics keeps completion_reason NULL.

rollback_plan: Revert the commit. No migration to reverse — job_outbox.completion_reason has existed since migration 083 and is nullable with no CHECK constraint, so historical rows carrying 'import_consent_blocked' are inert after a revert and no reader interprets them. No feature flag, no env var, no data backfill. The helper generalization reverts with the same commit, restoring markOutboxOwnerUnreachable at its two call sites (NotificationWorker.ts and the failover poller's integration suite).
observability: Operational-window signal (new), NOT an audit record: SELECT completion_reason, count(*) FROM job_outbox WHERE topic = 'zernio_initial_backfill' AND status = 'completed' GROUP BY 1 — an 'import_consent_blocked' bucket counts refusals. Trustworthy in exactly one band: rows created after deploy AND completed within the last 7 days. Two independent limits — (a) refusals from before this change are also NULL, so NULL means 'genuine import OR pre-deployment refusal'; (b) ArchivalPoller deletes completed job_outbox rows 7 days after completed_at, and a refusal completes rather than fails, so it takes the 7-day arm. Same life owner_unreachable has always had (ADR 0010) — a property of the sink, not of this ticket. The record that outlives the window is businesses.import_decision / import_decision_at.

Existing signal (unchanged): the structured worker log line 'import consent blocked — skipping backfill' carrying { reason, business_id } — the per-state detail the single marker deliberately does not duplicate, and the ONLY record of it when the businesses row is gone.
How I would know it broke — marker regression: a refusal that leaves completion_reason NULL (the pre-change behaviour) means the guard stopped stamping.

How I would know it broke — generalization regression: HealthAlertPoller.checkOwnerUnreachable and NotificationFailoverPoller going quiet, or send_notification rows completing with completion_reason NULL where the owner had zero verified enrollments, means owner_unreachable marking was lost in the refactor.
